A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM-Explorer work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Atari and MuJoCo training results, baseline comparisons, component ablations and sensitivity experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds computational-cost measurements, controlled comparisons and experiments on method variants in Section 4 and Appendices F–J.

M1.justification: The core two-LLM pipeline remains unchanged, but Appendices G–J substantially extend the evaluated procedures: multiple-episode inputs, reward-progress-triggered updates, automatic task descriptions, KL-based fallback safeguards and selection between two generated distributions. These are implemented experimental variants, rather than replacements for the default method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 15 Atari and five MuJoCo tasks. The additional experiments reuse this coverage. The reversed-starting-position scenarios in Appendix J.3 are hypothetical, not newly evaluated environments.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets are retained, including NoisyNet and RND in Appendix C and the RL algorithms in Figure 3. The added time-budget comparison reuses NoisyNet; Qwen models and safeguards are configurations or variants of LLM-Explorer.

E3.justification: V2 adds a wall-clock-matched comparison using 500k LLM-Explorer steps and additional NoisyNet training steps, plus evaluations varying Qwen model size, trajectory history, adaptive-update thresholds and prompting/safeguard configurations. It also introduces KL-based diagnostic metrics. These supplement the retained original training settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds model-size sensitivity, history-length tests, adaptive-update comparisons, automatic-description and template/example ablations, and failure diagnostics with safeguard experiments on Qbert and Seaquest. These investigate substantial new questions beyond the retained workflow and M/K ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions average three random seeds and report standard-deviation bands in learning curves. Added experiments follow the same averaging practice, without new confidence intervals or significance tests. The new KL summaries diagnose output skew rather than uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values, including the 37.27% mean Atari improvement, are retained. V2 adds extensive results under additional conditions: Table 8 reports Alien scores of 414.79 versus 377.64 for LLM-Explorer and time-matched NoisyNet; Table 13 reports Qbert scores of 316.92 with KL clip (old) versus 301.97 without safeguards. Cost, model-size, history and prompting results are also new.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation and equations (1)–(3) are retained. Neither version provides theoretical proofs. V2 adds empirical KL diagnostics and procedural heuristics, without new formal propositions, assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: adaptive LLM-guided exploration, plug-in compatibility across discrete and continuous RL algorithms, and performance improvement up to 37.27%. The additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 supplements the general hallucination limitation with specific skewed-output failure hypotheses and initial-state conditions under which state-agnostic guidance may fail. It adds interpretations of history, prompting and cost trade-offs, removes the speculation that GPT-4o is too sophisticated, and discusses capability limitations using the new Qwen-size results.

D1.justification: V2 adds per-task runtime and API-cost profiles, explicit prompts for automatic-description variants, and window/threshold settings for adaptive updates and safeguards. The original hardware and base hyperparameters remain. Documented code access changes from the anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Self-Consistency and Self-Refine, connecting them to the safeguard experiment and possible future mitigation. The existing references, related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Section 4 gains a computational-overhead subsection and revised trade-off organization; appendix headings and references are adjusted. V2 also adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist and updates author footnotes and conference identification.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial tabular displays for computational cost, model sizes, trajectory history, update scheduling, automatic descriptions, KL diagnostics and safeguards in Tables 1, 5 and 8–14. Existing tables are renumbered and some relocated; Figures 1–9 retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens assessment of practicality and reliability. V1 reported token consumption and left hallucination mitigation to future work; v2 adds runtime/API costs, an equal-wall-clock NoisyNet comparison, failure diagnostics and tested safeguards. The additional sensitivity and prompting studies clarify design choices and applicability. These gains outweigh minor new reporting inconsistencies, including the duplicated template-only description in Appendix I and conflicting Alien baseline values in Tables 7 and 9–10.
